Questions

Start from the question you need to answer. Each question points to the protocol for your pathogen, or to protocols that work together.

  • Are these cases related to each other?

    Find out whether cases share a recent common source or belong to the same transmission chain, using whole-genome relatedness.

    • VirusesViral phylogenomic surveillance
    • BacteriaBacterial phylogenomic surveillance
    • FungiFungal phylogenomic surveillance
  • When did this outbreak start, or when was the pathogen introduced?

    Estimate when a group of cases began, or when a lineage arrived, by dating its common ancestor with a molecular clock.

    • VirusesViral phylogenomic surveillance
    • BacteriaBacterial phylogenomic surveillance
    • FungiFungal phylogenomic surveillance
  • Was this introduced once, or several times?

    Tell apart a single introduction followed by local spread from repeated introductions from elsewhere.

    • VirusesViral phylogenomic surveillance
    • BacteriaBacterial phylogenomic surveillance
    • FungiFungal phylogenomic surveillance
  • Is drug resistance spreading between cases?

    Find out whether resistant infections share a resistant strain, or acquired resistance separately.

    • BacteriaAMR gene detection and tracking+Bacterial phylogenomic surveillance
    • FungiAntifungal resistance mutation detection+Fungal phylogenomic surveillance
  • Have segments of this virus reassorted?

    Detect whether a segmented virus, such as influenza, has exchanged genome segments with another strain.

    • VirusesViral phylogenomic surveillance
